C1.rule: Mechanical, one owned file, fully specified

C2.rule: Bounded implementation or tests, one or two owned files and their tests

C4.rule: Planning, merging, reconciling, another project's real data, a sponsor decision

phases.name: Mandatory standard
phases.goal: Every session the sponsor gives /standard follows one structure and speaks one language; the PhotoVault app and engine first.

items.title: Proposal template and bin/new-proposal
items.what: templates/proposal.html in the checked shape (status meta, <ol class="decisions">, id="decided" block, exceptions) and bin/new-proposal NN-or-next "title" writing the page and its ledger; proposalcheck and tracker validate pass on the result.
items.done: A new proposal in a scratch project passes proposalcheck and tracker validate unedited.

log.evidence: from origin/main f658e3e; owns templates/proposal.html, bin/new-proposal

514dccd on p21-s02. templates/proposal.html carries proposal-id, proposal-status proposed, and common-rules-template proposal/21; sections for the ask, findings, options and an <ol class="decisions">. bin/new-proposal picks the next free number (or a refused --number collision), makes an ASCII slug, refuses bad titles, creates both files without overwriting, runs proposalcheck and tracker validate, and removes both files if either rejects them. 26 tests red, then green; 803 OK.

The template ships no literal id="decided" or id="exceptions" attribute. proposalcheck only checks that the attribute exists, so an empty block in the template would let every page reach accepted with nothing recorded. A test pins that a generated page flipped to accepted fails.
probes: interplay with S-03's rule, numbering and races, atomicity, zero-item ledger through render, checkpoint and warmup, escaping, and the page rendered

Passed: escaping, atomicity (including SIGINT), a zero-item ledger through render, checkpoint and warmup, numbering refusals, and S-03 interplay for dated pages; the rendered page reads as a clear skeleton; 803 OK. Fix first: (1) an accepted page with no decided date passes both checkers; (2) the template never shows the literal meta lines; (3) a ledger without a page blocks its own number, so S-10 cannot make proposal 21's page; (4) a fresh proposal fails warmup --check (no tracker page); (5) a date-prefixed file jumps the number to 2027; (6) the app and engine appear to share one numbering series; (7) PermissionError gives a traceback; (8) a substring match blames the wrong file; (9) a race refusal says nothing about retrying; wording.

Round 2 rulings: date-first literal lines in the template, plus an expectedFailure flip test (the proposalcheck side goes to S-03); --page-for LEDGER; render the tracker page as part of the atomic write; numbers only ^\d{1,3}[a-z]?-; optional proposal_series declaration validated in tools/project.py; exit 2 with named errors; exact-name matching; a retry hint; wording fixes.

items.done: App 72/75/76 and engine 77 (added 13 Sep) do not newly fail; a new page without status does.

The S-02 reviewer found the wrong 'carries no proposal status' message on such a page.

asks.quote: Yes. This is mandatory. It's not optional. I want them to follow the same structure, and they should refactor once they reach the... they should tell me, okay, at what stage when the current tasks are finished, they will refactor it. And I want every... both of those sessions to speak the common language and handle things in the same way. It's mandatory. It's not optional.

And I want this to be a standard way of proceeding ahead for other projects as well whenever I create a session at a user level. I want the... once I use the command, I want the sessions to accept it and do whatever needs to be done to follow the standard way.

and make it in such a way if I improve something in the common rules in the future regarding warm up or reheat. Then the project should prioritize that and implement it. It's not optional. It needs to be implemented always, mandatory.
Common rules also works with the same workflow. So I would like you to maintain the same processes what we are implementing in other projects.
